description:
pkix-lint/src/lib.rs:135:

    // Re-export so callers only need to depend on pkix-lint, not pkix-path.
    pub use pkix_path::{Profile, ValidatedPath, ValidationPolicy};

This is convenience for callers but locks pkix-lint's public API to
pkix-path's major version. If pkix-path cuts 1.0 → 2.0 (e.g., changes
ValidatedPath to gain a new public field, or renames Profile method
signatures), every pkix-lint consumer's source breaks even if they
never touched the re-exported types directly.

Workspace-internal that is the intended shape: both crates live in
the same workspace, version together. But pkix-lint is published to
crates.io as a separate crate; downstream consumers who pin
`pkix-lint = \"0.9\"` will receive the *current* pkix-path version
transitively. When pkix-path bumps major, pkix-lint must bump major
too even when nothing in pkix-lint itself changed.

# What the caller cannot do

The caller has no way to insulate themselves from pkix-path major
bumps via pkix-lint. They cannot pin pkix-lint and float pkix-path
independently — pkix-lint locks the version.

# Options

1. Document the version-coupling: state explicitly in pkix-lint's
   public docs that pkix-path major bumps will force a pkix-lint
   major bump too. Callers can then make their dependency decision
   informed.

2. Re-export through your own newtype: define pkix_lint::Profile,
   pkix_lint::ValidatedPath, pkix_lint::ValidationPolicy as wrappers
   that delegate. This decouples versions but doubles the maintenance
   surface and forces callers to convert between types when bridging
   to pkix-chain.

3. Keep the re-export but version-pin pkix-path tightly (=0.5 or
   similar) in pkix-lint's Cargo.toml and bump both together as a
   workspace policy.

The current Cargo.toml uses `pkix-path = { workspace = true }`, which
defers the pin to the workspace root. That's the right structural
choice for now, but it should be made explicit that the workspace's
version-bump cadence applies to pkix-lint as a consequence.

Per AGENTS.md: 'Re-exports from upstream crates that lock the major
version. If you `pub use foo::Bar` and `foo` cuts a major version,
your crate's API is broken too. Either re-export through your own
newtype or document the upstream version pin.'

Cheapest fix: document the coupling. Verdict P2 because the
workspace ships both crates as a unit and the coupling is intentional
under the workspace stance, but the contract should state it.
title: API contract: re-exporting pkix_path::{Profile, ValidatedPath, ValidationPolicy} couples major versions
